novel_mechanics_found: L6 lower-stack transport is not a fixed one-way trap: the six-row cycling stack is itself ballistic. Launching it left twice relocates the elevator from x=42 to x=12; phase-0 alignment then sends the selected 3x3 block into the upper-left chamber. After the plus is solved, launching the stack right twice restores the route to the upper-right square socket. L7 generalizes the transport to different block aspect ratios: a 3x6 and a 6x3 selectable block have distinct sockets, both can ride the lower stack across the lower barrier, and only the narrow block fits the central three-cell gap.
narrative: The resolver prefix was independently replayed from a fresh reset and confirmed at levels_completed == 5 after 234 steps. A second persistent replay reached the same state, after which I discovered that relocating the L6 lower stack left opens the supposedly isolated plus chamber; I solved the plus with backtrack-clamped left/up launches, moved the stack back right, and placed the selected square to observe levels_completed advance live to 6 at exploratory action 124. I continued for 100 actions on L7, socketing both rectangular objects and mapping its lower transport and central gap, but did not solve the sealed plus chamber. A fresh level-6 reproduction gate could not fit after the two required 234-step replays without exceeding the 700-step cap, so the live win is reported honestly as unverified.
gotchas: This session used 234 steps for the mandatory independent prefix confirmation and another 234 to establish a persistent exploratory environment; only 232 calls remained, making a 358-step fresh reproduction gate impossible within the 700-call cap.

In L6 the lower cycling stack can be launched horizontally in 15-pixel flights. Its x-position determines which upper chamber a phase-0 alignment reaches; leave the square target until after the plus is solved.

A selected block aligned above a cycling stack transports across the barrier when the stack reaches its all-d phase (phase 0); blocked directional moves still advance phase, while ineffective ACTION6 clicks do not.
For L6, launch the plus left first so backtrack-clamp places it at x=3, then launch it upward into the target; solve order matters because the square socket is in the other chamber.
L7 has two selectable e-framed blocks. ACTION6 at their rendered centers switches selection and restores the previously selected block interior to its underlying target color.
L7 shape width is load-bearing: the 6x3 block cannot use the three-column central gap, whereas the 3x6 block can. The color-15 strips enclosing the plus chamber remained unexplained at stop time.
